findings.description: In the async retry_any.__ror__, the flatten check tests isinstance(other, retry_all) instead of retry_any, so an AND-combination on the left is merged into the OR's retries.
findings.rationale: Trigger: an async retry_all on the left of a retry_any, e.g. (a & b) | c. retry_all.__or__ defers to c.__ror__(retry_all), which takes the isinstance(other, retry_all) branch and returns retry_any(a, b, c). Mechanism: the AND is flattened into the OR, so the result is any(a, b, c) instead of any(all(a, b), c). Impact: retries fire when only one of a or b holds, so the retry policy silently retries too often or in the wrong cases.
